screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article summarizing literature on drug-induced liver injury, not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment. Does not meet study design criteria.
This study investigates aspirin absorption during migraine, not paracetamol. The intervention does not match the review focus on paracetamol.
This is an epidemiological study analyzing paracetamol sales and overdose/suicide trends, not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This is a Cochrane review about aspirin for migraine, not paracetamol. Also, it is a systematic review, not a primary clinical trial.

This appears to be a randomized controlled trial comparing DHE+paracetamol combination vs individual drugs vs placebo for acute migraine. Includes paracetamol monotherapy arm. 288 patients evaluated. While double-blinding is not explicitly stated, the study design with placebo control and multiple treatment arms suggests rigorous methodology. Conservative approach warrants inclusion.
This is a population-based epidemiological survey on headache prevalence in China, not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This is a methodological paper about assessing quality of RCT reports and the effect of rater blinding, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological paper about conducting meta-analyses of cross-over trials, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis of pharmacological treatments for acute migraine, not a primary randomized controlled trial of paracetamol.
This is an epidemiological telephone survey on headache and migraine prevalence in Germany, not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This is an epidemiological study analyzing migraine prevalence by age and sex in the US population, not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.

This is a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel group study investigating a fixed combination containing paracetamol (200mg) for headache/migraine treatment. Also includes paracetamol monotherapy arm (500mg). 1743 patients enrolled. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article discussing the mechanism of action of paracetamol, not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This is a methodological chapter from a handbook about assessing risk of bias in studies, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a paper describing the development of a database of RCTs in pain research, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, three-way cross-over trial comparing paracetamol (1g) alone vs paracetamol + domperidone (antiemetic) 20mg vs paracetamol + domperidone 30mg for migraine treatment. 46 patients completed. Directly addresses paracetamol with antiemetic co-therapy. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a statistical methodology paper about calculating confidence intervals, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This is a methodological paper about pain intensity scales and VAS interpretation, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, crossover, multicenter phase III clinical trial comparing etodolac (400mg and 800mg) vs paracetamol (1000mg) for acute migraine treatment. 229 adult patients included. Paracetamol is used as an active comparator. Meets all selection criteria.
This study investigates the effect of metoclopramide on aspirin absorption during migraine, not paracetamol. The intervention does not match the review focus on paracetamol.
This is a literature review about paracetamol poisoning/overdose and pack size restrictions, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment. Wrong study type and wrong topic.

Randomized crossover trial comparing domperidone+paracetamol (Domperamol) with sumatriptan for moderate to severe migraine. 120 patients recruited. Tests paracetamol with antiemetic for migraine treatment. Meets criteria for paracetamol+antiemetic combination. Conservative inclusion recommended.
Only 14 patients total (below 10 per arm threshold). Uses IV metoclopramide alone without paracetamol. Not self-administered (IV in emergency department). Does not meet intervention criteria.
Methodological paper about meta-analysis in clinical research. Not a primary clinical trial. Wrong study type.
Cross-sectional survey estimating economic costs of headache disorders in Europe. Not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine. Wrong study type and topic.

Double-blind, three-way crossover trial comparing isometheptene+acetaminophen+dichloralphenazone (Midrin) with acetaminophen alone and placebo. 56 adult migraineurs. Includes acetaminophen alone arm. Self-administered oral medication. Meets criteria for paracetamol treatment of migraine.
Observational survey describing patterns of migraine treatment in the US. Not a randomized controlled trial. Wrong study design.
Basic science/mechanism paper about prostaglandin synthetase inhibition by paracetamol. Not a clinical trial for migraine treatment. Wrong study type.

Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study in 5 healthy volunteers, not migraine patients. Investigates COX-2 inhibition mechanism. Not a clinical trial for migraine treatment. Wrong population and study type.
Review article about migraine diagnosis and underdiagnosis. Not a clinical trial. Wrong study type.
Commentary/review article about COX-3 and paracetamol mechanism of action. Not a clinical trial. Wrong study type.
Abstract describes fungal infection research (Rhizopus/Pseudomonas), completely unrelated to migraine or paracetamol. Title does not match abstract content. Wrong topic.
Epidemiological study analyzing years lived with disability across diseases globally. Not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine. Wrong study type.

Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial of acetaminophen 1000mg for episodic migraine headache. 346 adult patients (177 acetaminophen, 169 placebo). Self-administered oral medication. Clearly meets all selection criteria.
Systematic review about paracetamol safety in alcoholic patients, not a primary clinical trial for migraine. Focuses on hepatic injury risk, not migraine efficacy. Wrong study type and topic.
Telephone survey about patient preferences for migraine therapy. Not a randomized controlled trial. Wrong study design.
Editorial/commentary about Global Burden of Disease findings. Not a clinical trial. Wrong study type.
Methodological study about duplicate publication in meta-analysis, focused on ondansetron for postoperative emesis. Not a paracetamol migraine trial. Wrong topic and study type.
Review article about paracetamol hepatotoxicity and therapeutic misadventure. Not a clinical trial for migraine treatment. Wrong study type and topic.
Randomized double-blind trial comparing IV metoclopramide with subcutaneous sumatriptan for migraine. No paracetamol in either treatment arm. Does not meet intervention criteria.
This is an epidemiological survey studying prevalence of headache disorders in Russia. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.
This is a literature review summarizing headache epidemiology studies in Europe. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled crossover study comparing tolfenamic acid with paracetamol (500mg and 1000mg) for treating common migraine. 83 patients were enrolled across 4 treatment arms, meeting the minimum of 10 participants per arm. Paracetamol was self-administered to treat acute migraine episodes.

This is a longitudinal survey study examining economic burden and healthcare resource utilization in transformed migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.
This is a clinical practice guideline providing expert recommendations for migraine treatment. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is an overview paper discussing epidemiological evidence and disability measurement for migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a before-and-after observational study examining the effects of pack size restrictions on paracetamol self-poisoning. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a double-blind controlled study comparing Paramax (paracetamol 0.5g + metoclopramide 5mg) with placebo for acute migraine treatment. 49 patients were enrolled, suggesting approximately 25 per arm, meeting the minimum of 10 participants per arm. Paracetamol was self-administered to treat acute migraine episodes.
This is a systematic literature review and recommendations paper about OTC drugs for migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.
This is a basic science/molecular biology study describing COX-3 protein cloning and expression. It is not a clinical trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment in humans.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 4 treatment arms including acetaminophen alone (1000mg). 173 patients treated migraines, with approximately 43 patients per arm, meeting the minimum of 10 participants per arm. Acetaminophen was self-administered to treat acute migraine episodes.

This is a methodological/statistical paper discussing trial size requirements and random effects in clinical trials. It is not a randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a population-based survey study examining disability profiles and treatment patterns in chronic migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a narrative review discussing the economic burden and disease management of migraine in the US. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.
This is a clinical practice guide/review article providing recommendations for migraine management. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a review article discussing the mechanism of action of acetaminophen and potential COX-3 involvement. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a population-based survey study examining migraine prevalence and preventive therapy patterns in the US. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a population-based survey study examining migraine recognition and treatment patterns in France. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing oral acetaminophen 1000mg with placebo for treating single acute migraine attacks. The study design indicates sufficient participants per arm (population-based study). Acetaminophen was self-administered to treat acute migraine episodes.

This is a cross-sectional economic analysis study examining healthcare costs for migraine patients in five European countries. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for acute migraine treatment.

This study investigates the pharmacokinetics of aspirin (ASA), not paracetamol (acetaminophen). The selection criteria specifically require studies using self-administered paracetamol to treat acute migraine. While the study is randomised and involves migraine patients, the intervention drug is aspirin (900 mg) with or without metoclopramide, not paracetamol. The outcomes measured are pharmacokinetic parameters (absorption rates, elimination rates, plasma levels) rather than clinical efficacy outcomes for migraine treatment. This is a fundamental mismatch with the review's intervention criteria.
